To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) the flow of water over bedforms in the upper sedimentary layer of rivers induces significant convective flow in the pore water; 2) convective flow in this layer can be enhanced by a factor of 2-10 compared to that induced by temperature gradients alone; 3) convective flow is enhanced in regions of the river with low sediment grain size; and, 4) the effect is most important in regions where bedform height and spacing are greatest.
bedform-generated convective flow in bed sediment may be significant and that it may enhance the transport of chemicals and thermal energy in the bed sediment.
bedforms generate convective transport within the sediment layer.
